main_text.l: quam vitam intuendam, indeque de eo formandum iudicium : alioqui enim multa scelera, quæ clam patrantur, mansura impunita: imitandosque heic Areopagitas, qui deficientibus testibus, & non obstante ornata & speciosa rei defensione ex conscientia sua, & diligenti inquisitione, sæpè iudicium ferre solent. Ubi inter alia hæc verba habet: Quis enim aut graffator, aut fur, aut adulter, aut homicida, aut gravissimorum scelerum designator, modo occulte facinus patret, pœnas dabit? Inter hos enim ii, qui in ipso facinore deprehenduntur, & fatentur, statim occiduntur: qui autem clam patrarunt, & inficiantur, in iudicium adducuntur: deque iis, veritas verisimilibus coniecturis est[?] indaganda. Eamus longius. Lex erat Athenis, ut, qui ærario aut diis multam debebant, si intra præscriptum tempus non solverent, in vinculis haberentur, quoad solverent. Hanc firmabat lex alia, quâ sanciebatur, ne cui referre liceret de restituendis honori ignominiosis (ἀτίμωσις[?]) aut de remittenda multa debitoribus ærarii, deorumque, nisi prius decreto suo potestatem ejus rei dedissent Atheniensium sex millibus haud pauciores, idque per suffragia occulta: tum demum liceret,

page.notes: Catchword "quate" is cut off at the foot of the page and only partly legible; the [?] marks the doubt. The Greek word after "honori ignominiosis" is faint; I read it as ἀτίμωσις, but the accents and letters are doubtful. "esl" before "indaganda" is read as "est" with [?]. The long s in "sex" and "Atheniensium" is printed as a long s and is written here as plain s. The right edge carries show-through from the facing page (stray marks and letters), which is not transcribed.
